newsitem.title: SPAIN: ETA suspected in northern Spain grenade attack.
newsitem.headline: ETA suspected in northern Spain grenade attack.

text.p: Two grenades exploded near a police station on Monday, injuring one person, in what authorities believe was the first attack by Basque separatist guerrillas since they killed a Spanish politician earlier this month.
The attack, using grenade launchers, targeted the National Police station in the northern Spanish city of Oviedo.

But the grenades missed the station, with one exploding on the patio of a nearby building and the other hitting a street, officials said. A woman was slightly injured and was treated at a local hospital and released.
The incident in Oviedo, the capital of the Asturias region, occurred just over a week after ETA rebels sparked national outrage by killing Basque town councillor Miguel Angel Blanco.
A government source said ETA was suspected in the grenade attack but added that the incident was still under investigation.
Police cordoned off the area and found a third unexploded grenade which they rendered harmless. They also found two grenade launchers used in the attack. No arrests were made.
